methodological_rigor.justification: The single-arm phase 2 design is appropriate for a rare tumor subtype (desmoplastic melanoma), and the pre-specified primary endpoint (pCR by local pathology) is justified with an explicit power calculation (n=25, 90% power, one-sided alpha 3.4%, null pCR 5% vs alternative 25%) using an exact Clopper-Pearson binomial test. Pre-specified secondary and exploratory endpoints (central pathology review, WES) were defined, and analyses handled nonresponders conservatively (patients without surgery counted as nonresponders). Appropriate time-to-event methods are used: Kaplan-Meier with log-log CIs for RFS/OS and Nelson-Aalen with Pintilie CIs for melanoma-specific survival treating other-cause death as competing risk. Acknowledged limitations include absence of a control arm, local pathology as primary endpoint (mitigated by exploratory central review with high concordance), small sample size limiting subgroup inference, and no formal multiplicity adjustment for exploratory analyses.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual single-arm phase 2 cohort study (non-randomized), mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high: desmoplastic melanoma is a rare, surgically morbid subtype typically affecting elderly patients (median age 75), and the demonstrated 71% pCR rate with manageable toxicity (7% grade 3, no grade 4/5) provides prospective evidence supporting neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 that could reduce surgical morbidity and spare adjuvant therapy. Endpoints include patient-relevant outcomes (OS 87%, RFS 74%, melanoma-specific survival 95% at 3 years), and the findings directly inform management of an understudied subtype, though the single-arm design and small n prevent definitive practice-change without a randomized comparison.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable standard for this prospective single-arm trial; the manuscript includes a CONSORT diagram (Fig. 1), pre-registration on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02775851), explicit pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints, sample-size justification, enrollment dates, eligibility criteria, adverse event reporting using CTCAE v4.03, and ethics approval statements. The protocol is referenced in Supplementary Information. Minor gaps include lack of explicit per-item CONSORT checklist, no formal post-hoc designation for melanoma-specific survival beyond a brief note, and the reporting-summary file is referenced but not visible. Source data for figures are noted and a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced, but there is no explicit statement in the blinded text that whole-exome sequencing data have been deposited in a public repository with an accession identifier, limiting the data-availability score.

novelty_literature.justification: This represents the first prospective phase 2 trial of neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 monotherapy specifically in resectable desmoplastic melanoma, a rare and understudied subtype traditionally enrolled only within larger cutaneous melanoma trials where its signal could be diluted. It builds on and prospectively validates the retrospective Eroglu 2018 observation of high anti-PD-1 responsiveness in advanced desmoplastic melanoma (ref 2) and complements the companion cohort B publication (ref 8) in unresectable disease. Novelty is population- and empirical-based rather than mechanistic; the broader neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 paradigm is already established by SWOG S1801 and NADINA (refs 6, 17), so the contribution is a focused subtype-specific extension with correlative genomic analysis (NF1, TP53, CDKN2A, high TMB) rather than a conceptually new finding.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and logically organized: the Main/Introduction sets up the rationale around rarity, surgical morbidity, and known PD-1 responsiveness; Methods are detailed; Results map cleanly to pre-specified endpoints; and the Discussion situates findings against comparator neoadjuvant trials with explicit numeric benchmarks. The abstract is self-contained and quantitatively grounded (pCR 71%, 95% CI 51-87%, P<0.001, 2 grade-3 AEs, 3-year follow-up). Figure and table captions are informative and standalone-interpretable (CONSORT, schema, waterfall, swimmer-style outcomes, KM curves, oncoprint). Minor issues: Table 1 content is run together in the markdown rendering, some sections (e.g., central pathology review) are long and could be tightened, and acronyms are generally defined but pCR/pPR definitions could appear earlier.

key_strengths: Pre-specified primary endpoint with explicit power calculation (90% power, null 5% vs alternative 25%) formally met with 71% pCR (95% CI 51-87%, P<0.001)
First prospective phase 2 trial of neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 monotherapy focused specifically on desmoplastic melanoma, a rare and surgically morbid subtype
Rigorous correlative work including blinded central pathology review (high local/central concordance) and WES with TMB and driver-gene analyses as pre-specified exploratory endpoints
Mature 42-month median follow-up with appropriate competing-risk analysis for melanoma-specific survival (95% at 3 years) and favorable safety profile (only 2 grade-3 AEs, no grade 4/5)
Transparent reporting with CONSORT diagram, pre-registration (NCT02775851), and conservative handling of non-resected or inadequately assessed patients as nonresponders
key_concerns: Single-arm design and small sample (n=28) preclude causal/comparative inference; cross-trial pCR comparisons in the Discussion should be framed cautiously
Primary endpoint relies on local pathology review; central review was exploratory and not available for all surgical specimens (24/28)
Explicit data-availability statement for whole-exome sequencing data (repository, accession) is not visible in the blinded text
No formal multiplicity correction for the multiple exploratory analyses (subgroup, genomic, central vs local pathology)
Enrollment is predominantly white (96%) and heavily head-and-neck (68%), limiting generalizability and precluding meaningful subgroup inference
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically sound, prospectively conducted, pre-registered phase 2 trial that met its pre-specified primary endpoint in a rare and clinically important melanoma subtype, with mature follow-up and robust correlative work; the combination of clinical importance, novelty of the focused population, and reporting rigor supports plausible acceptance at a top-tier oncology/general-medicine journal with minor revisions to clarify data availability and temper cross-trial comparisons.
